chunks: Mu'āwiyah ibn 'Ammār and Abū Baṣīr narrated from Abū 'Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
The boundary of Minā extends from al-'Aqabah to Wādī Muḥassir, and the boundary of 'Arafāt extends from al-Ma'zimayn to the farthest point of the standing place.

key_terms.الْعَقَبَةِ: al-'Aqabah, the point marking one end of Minā
key_terms.الْمَوْقِفِ: the standing place, referring to the area of wuqūf in 'Arafāt
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: 'Arafāt, the sacred plain of standing during hajj
key_terms.مِنًى: Minā, one of the sacred ritual locations of hajj
key_terms.وَادِي مُحَسِّرٍ: Wādī Muḥassir, the valley marking the other end of Minā

ai.seo_question: What are the boundaries of Minā and 'Arafāt in hajj according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith defines the legal boundaries of two major hajj sites: Minā and 'Arafāt. Its significance lies in clarifying the geographical limits relevant to the rites of pilgrimage and the validity of standing and presence in those sacred locations.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2978 - Mu'awiyah ibn Ammar and Abu Basir narrated from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:
"The boundary of Mina extends from Al-Aqabah to the Valley of Muhassir, and the boundary of Arafat extends from Al-Mazameen to the farthest point of the standing area (Mawqif)."
